summary: The output component is the loop's single managed stdout stream. It holds one global OUTPUT_LOCK so concurrent tasks never interleave, and a set of atomic suppression flags (compact, verbose, quiet, json, streaming, plain, tui-active) that decide whether a given emission is rendered, reshaped, or dropped. It records TokenUsage counters, produces semantic tool-call summaries, prints diffs, progress phases, thinking, and final answers. On the loop it is a downstream perceive surface: it projects loop state to a human or a machine, and its suppression rules are the foundation that keeps other components (TUI, JSON consumers) uncorrupted.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with output read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where every print funnels through OUTPUT_LOCK and should_suppress_output() gates the TUI/JSON/quiet modes.

examples.title: Serialize all emission through OUTPUT_LOCK
examples.intent: Guarantee that concurrent loop tasks never tear each other's lines on stdout.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Every print acquires the global mutex before writing, so parallel act steps and streaming tokens serialize into one clean channel; it never blocks the loop's control, only orders its output.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the OutputStream node shows the lock's current holder and a queue of pending writers.
touch_interaction.visual: Node shows a single lit gate; contending writers stack as dimmed chips waiting their turn.

examples.mini_scenario: Two sub-agents finish at once; both grab OUTPUT_LOCK in turn, so their summaries print whole rather than interleaved.
examples.pitfall: A panic while holding the lock must recover via into_inner() — the code does this; don't replace it with unwrap().

examples.title: Suppress human output in JSON mode
examples.intent: Keep stdout valid JSON when a machine consumes the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_json_mode(true) makes banners, 'Final answer:' prefixes, and ANSI escapes no-ops, so only structured payloads leave the loop; it reshapes the perceive channel by mode.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the mode switch cycles the OutputStream between human, compact, quiet, and JSON facets.
touch_interaction.visual: Node badge flips to a { } glyph; decorative sub-nodes (banners, emoji) grey out.

examples.mini_scenario: Run with --json; the final answer prints as raw content only, safe for a downstream parser.
examples.pitfall: final_answer must strip its prefix in json/plain mode — a stray 'Final answer:' breaks the parser.

examples.title: Detect a non-TTY and drop to plain mode
examples.intent: Avoid emitting ANSI/emoji into a pipe or file.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: init() probes stdout_is_tty(); if false it sets PLAIN_MODE and disables colored overrides, so the loop's output degrades gracefully for captured runs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the OutputStream node reveals the detected terminal capabilities and forces plain if desired.
touch_interaction.visual: When plain, the node loses its color swatches and renders in monochrome.

examples.mini_scenario: Selfware is piped into a log file; PLAIN_MODE strips escape codes so the log stays readable.
examples.pitfall: Probe once at init — re-checking mid-run can flip colors after the terminal has already been decorated.

examples.title: Emit a semantic summary per ToolCall
examples.intent: Turn a raw tool result into a one-line human read of the act.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: semantic_summary maps the ToolCall name+args+result to a compact phrase (e.g. 'Read foo.rs (120 lines)'), giving the loop's act trace meaning without dumping raw JSON.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a summarized tool node expands to show the raw args and result behind the phrase.
touch_interaction.visual: Summary chip carries a tool-family icon and a green/red status dot from the success flag.

examples.mini_scenario: A grep returns 12 matches; the summary reads "Searched 'todo' (12 matches)" instead of a match array.
examples.pitfall: The fallback arm must still render unknown tools — never return an empty string for an unmapped name.

examples.title: Skip re-printing when streaming is live
examples.intent: Avoid printing the answer twice when tokens already streamed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: final_answer checks is_streaming_mode() and returns early, so the loop's terminal emission isn't duplicated after live token display.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the answer node while streaming shows the live token feed instead of a static block.
touch_interaction.visual: During stream the node pulses per-token; on completion it seals without a second render.

examples.mini_scenario: Tokens stream live to the screen; at Completed, final_answer no-ops so the text isn't repeated.
examples.pitfall: If you disable streaming you must re-enable the final print, or the answer never appears.

examples.title: Record TokenUsage into session counters
examples.intent: Accumulate prompt/completion tokens so the loop knows its spend.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: record_tokens atomically adds to the session totals that Budget-aware UI and /stats read; it feeds the loop's budget picture without gating it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the token node shows cumulative prompt/completion and a per-turn delta.
touch_interaction.visual: A rolling counter animates upward on each turn; color shifts as spend accelerates.

examples.mini_scenario: After a turn the loop calls record_tokens(1200, 380); the sticky bar's total ticks to 1.58K.
examples.pitfall: Reset counters only on a new session — mid-run reset_tokens() corrupts the budget read.

examples.title: Print a color-coded DiffView on edit
examples.intent: Let the operator see exactly what an edit changes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: display_file_diff runs an LCS-style diff of old vs new content and prints ± lines, giving the verify stage a visible artifact — but it returns early under TUI/compact/quiet/json.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading over the diff node expands the ± hunks into a full panel capped at the max display lines.
touch_interaction.visual: Added lines green, deleted red; a '… more changes' chip appears when the cap is hit.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit changes 5 lines; the loop prints a green/red diff block before the write is announced.
examples.pitfall: The diff caps at max_diff_lines to avoid flooding — don't remove the cap or huge edits swamp the frame.

examples.title: Drive the multi-phase progress bar
examples.intent: Show staged progress with an ETA as the plan advances.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: TaskProgress transitions PhaseStatus and prints a bar; complete_phase advances the cursor, mirroring the loop's step machine and estimating remaining time from elapsed/progress.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging along the phase bar previews each phase's status and the computed ETA.
touch_interaction.visual: Filled cyan blocks for done work, dimmed blocks ahead; ETA chip updates as progress accrues.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop calls start_phase then complete_phase across three steps; the bar climbs 0→33→66→100% with a shrinking ETA.
examples.pitfall: estimated_remaining only computes above 5% progress — don't show an ETA on an unstarted plan.

examples.title: Gate thinking output to keep frames clean
examples.intent: Stream reasoning without corrupting the TUI or JSON output.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: thinking() short-circuits under compact/quiet/json/tui and rewrites \n to \r\n so inline reasoning resets to column 0; it exposes the reason stage safely.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the reasoning node toggles inline thinking visibility for the current turn.
touch_interaction.visual: Dimmed italic text streams in; in verbose it brightens with a 💭 marker.

examples.mini_scenario: The model thinks aloud; thinking() prints dimmed text inline, but in TUI mode it silently drops.
examples.pitfall: Raw \n in thinking text bleeds across TUI borders — the \r\n replacement is load-bearing.

examples.title: Announce a step at each plan boundary
examples.intent: Mark each numbered step as the driver crosses it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: step_start prints a step banner, suppressed under should_suppress_output(); it reflects the loop's Planning→Executing progression.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking across step banners scrubs the step history for the current run.
touch_interaction.visual: Each step prints with a 📝 badge and the step name in bright white.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop enters step 2; step_start prints '📝 Step 2: edit files...'.
examples.pitfall: Step banners are suppressed in machine modes — never parse them as protocol.

examples.title: Log a phase transition in verbose mode
examples.intent: Surface state-machine moves for debugging.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: phase_transition prints 'from → to' only when verbose and not quiet, exposing the loop's control transitions without noise in normal runs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the control node reveals the transition log for the run.
touch_interaction.visual: A 🔄 arrow animates from the old state chip to the new one.

examples.mini_scenario: In verbose mode the loop logs 'Executing → ErrorRecovery' when a tool fails.
examples.pitfall: This is verbose-only — don't rely on it as the source of truth for state; the agent owns that.

examples.title: Print token usage summary on demand
examples.intent: Show prompt+completion totals when the operator opts in.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: print_token_usage renders the split only when should_show_tokens() and not quiet/json; a perceive-only budget readout.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the budget node prints the prompt/completion/total breakdown for the turn.
touch_interaction.visual: In compact it shows '[N tokens]' dimmed; in normal a 📊 line with cyan numbers.

examples.mini_scenario: With --show-tokens the loop prints '📊 Tokens: 1200 prompt + 380 completion = 1580 total'.
examples.pitfall: Respect json/quiet suppression here — a token line in JSON mode corrupts the payload.

examples.title: Show the smart-fallback auto action
examples.intent: Tell the operator what the loop auto-decided to do after a no-action turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: smart_fallback_action prints the tool the recovery picked; it narrates an act the driver injected to keep the loop moving.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the auto-action node shows the chosen tool and a preview of its args.
touch_interaction.visual: A ↪ Auto chip in cyan names the tool with dimmed args.

examples.mini_scenario: The model described intent but didn't act; the fallback prints '↪ Auto: file_read {path:...}' and proceeds.
examples.pitfall: Suppressed in TUI/compact/quiet/json — don't make recovery visibility depend solely on this line.

examples.title: Render a verification report by outcome
examples.intent: Show a concise pass or a full failure report.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: verification_report prints a one-line pass in normal mode but always shows failures in full, tightening the verify stage's signal.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the verify node expands a passed check into the full report text.
touch_interaction.visual: Pass renders a green '✓ Verification passed'; failure prints the full report regardless of mode.

examples.mini_scenario: Tests pass; the loop prints '✓ Verification passed'. When they fail, the whole report is shown.
examples.pitfall: Failures must never be swallowed by compact mode — the code always prints them; preserve that.

examples.title: Emit gated debug turn dumps
examples.intent: Dump per-turn LLM responses only when the debug channel is on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: debug_output honors the DebugConfig 'turns' channel (or verbose) so raw turn content is available for diagnosis without polluting normal runs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the debug node toggles the turns channel and streams raw responses.
touch_interaction.visual: A magenta '=== DEBUG ===' frame wraps the dumped content.

examples.mini_scenario: Run with --debug=turns; each turn's raw LLM text prints between magenta debug fences.
examples.pitfall: Quiet mode still suppresses debug — don't assume --debug overrides --quiet.

examples.title: Print a safety-blocked notice
examples.intent: Tell the operator a tool was blocked by safety.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: safety_blocked prints a 🚫 line, but returns early under suppression because the block is also delivered via the agent event path in TUI mode.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the blocked node shows the safety reason and the offending command.
touch_interaction.visual: A red 🚫 badge marks the tool node; it does not proceed to act.

examples.mini_scenario: A destructive shell command trips the checker; the loop prints '🚫 blocked: rm -rf /' and skips it.
examples.pitfall: In TUI mode this stdout path is suppressed on purpose — rely on the event path there, not this print.

examples.title: Collapse to compact single-line progress
examples.intent: Fit the loop's status into one line for terse runs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: In compact mode print_progress emits '[pct% phase ETA:..]' on one line, compressing the perceive channel for low-noise environments.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-out collapses the multi-phase bar into a single compact status line.
touch_interaction.visual: One-line '[66% write ETA:~4s]' replaces the full phase list.

examples.mini_scenario: In --compact the loop shows '[66% write ETA:~4s]' instead of a five-line phase block.
examples.pitfall: Compact still divides by phase count — guard the empty-phase case to avoid a 0% 'Done' loop.

examples.title: Strip emoji and ANSI in plain mode
examples.intent: Produce clean text for terminals or logs that can't render decoration.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Plain-mode branches across print functions swap glyphs for ASCII and drop ANSI, so the perceive channel stays legible when captured.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the OutputStream node forces plain rendering for a copy-friendly view.
touch_interaction.visual: Progress icons become o/*/+/x; colors flatten to monochrome.

examples.mini_scenario: Piped to a CI log, phase icons render as o/*/+/x with no escape codes.
examples.pitfall: Every decorated print needs a plain branch — a missed one leaks escape codes into the log.

examples.title: Announce a task-completed banner
examples.intent: Signal a clean finish for entry points that want a generic banner.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: task_completed prints a success banner (suppressed in quiet/compact/json); the main path uses the failure-mode classifier, so this is a fallback terminal marker.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the completion node shows the finish banner and total elapsed.
touch_interaction.visual: A green '✅ Task completed successfully!' seals the run.

examples.mini_scenario: A generic entry point finishes and prints '✅ Task completed successfully!'.
examples.pitfall: The main agent path uses failure_mode::cli_banner instead — don't double-print completion.

examples.title: Yield the stream to the TUI renderer
examples.intent: Make output a no-op while the TUI owns the frame.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_tui_active(true) causes should_suppress_output() to short-circuit prints, handing the loop's perceive channel to the single TUI renderer.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the handoff node routes all emission into the TUI surface node.
touch_interaction.visual: The OutputStream node dims and an arrow points to the TUI node now doing the rendering.

examples.mini_scenario: The TUI launches; every output print becomes a no-op so the frame renders uncorrupted.
examples.pitfall: Reset the flag on TUI exit, or all subsequent CLI output stays silently suppressed.
